_readme: The declared-depth member-matching rule, as CASES — the one authority FOUR
implementations answer to.
The rule is implemented in Rust (`dataset/repository.rs::matches_member`, which the
server actually runs), mirrored in TypeScript so the upload wizard can tell the user
which member bound to which file BEFORE transferring anything
(`ui/src/modules/datasets/components/memberMatch.ts`), mirrored again in Python by a
contributed package's own container test, and a FOURTH time — basename-only — by a
sibling package's. Nothing made those agree.
A mirror that drifts WIDER promises an upload the server then refuses; a mirror that
drifts NARROWER silently blocks a valid upload in the panel, with no server-side
signal at all. This file makes either one a RED test on every side.
It lives beside the Rust source because that is where the authority is: a change to
the core that this file does not describe fails the core's own unit test first.
Every fixture here is deliberately vendor-neutral — the rule is generic over NESTING,
and a case table full of one vendor's filenames would be a claim about more than that.
`cases` pins the per-(file, member) PREDICATE. `groups` pins the DECISION — the whole
member set against a whole upload, which is where the one-bundle-root rule lives and
where a mirror that implements only the predicate is silently WIDER than the core.
That gap was real: the client mirror shipped without the root rule and would have
promised an upload the server then refused, for a bundle whose size is the reason the
folder picker exists.

cases.why: the depth-1 base case
a depth-1 member matches anywhere in the path
ONE compression suffix comes off the last segment
exactly one suffix, never two
ASCII case folding
ASCII-only folding: U+212A is not lowered
a K=2 member, exactly
anchored at the SUFFIX, so the run root is irrelevant
a sibling directory is not the declared one
fewer segments than the member declares
a missing intermediate segment is not skipped
both separators are honoured
interior empty segments are dropped
a name ending in a separator names a DIRECTORY
and a directory never has a compression suffix stripped
the suffix comes off the LAST segment only
the first alternative, at its own depth
the second alternative, at ITS own depth
the deeper alternative is not satisfied by a bare name
an empty declaration matches nothing, never everything
a separator-only declaration is empty too
and so is an alternation of nothing

groups.name: one bundle, members at one depth
groups.why: every member resolves once, all under one root

groups.name: one bundle, members at DIFFERENT depths inside it
groups.why: roots are ['outs','sub'] and ['outs'] — a CHAIN, which is one bundle with a loosely-declared member sitting deeper. Equality would refuse this.

groups.name: members gathered from TWO different bundles
groups.why: each member resolves once and nothing is ambiguous; only WHERE they came from is wrong

groups.name: members gathered from THREE different bundles
groups.why: the motivating case: three resolutions of three different specimens

groups.name: the root rule does NOT apply to a bare-basename declaration
groups.why: every container that shipped before #160 declares basenames; gathering those from different directories is behaviour nothing asked to change

groups.name: one file claiming two members
groups.why: an ambiguous DECLARATION, not a bad upload

groups.name: extra files beside a complete set are ignored
groups.why: a file matching no member is not a member and is not an error

groups.name: a BARE member is not held to the bundle root
groups.why: the deep members chain; the bare one declared that it does not care where it sits, so holding it to the root would refuse a legitimate bundle

groups.name: ONE deep member cannot disagree with itself
groups.why: a stated LIMIT of the rule, not an oversight: with a single path-carrying member there is nothing to compare it against

groups.name: two deep members under a COMMON PARENT are still two bundles
groups.why: a rule comparing only the first segment would group them

groups.name: a mixed-depth alternation roots at its DEEPEST match, not its first
groups.why: the first alternative also matches; taking it would root at [run,geo] vs [run] and make the verdict depend on declaration order

groups.name: one compression suffix comes off, in a group
groups.why: the suffix list is shared by four implementations and is otherwise unpinned at the group level

groups.name: a declaration with an EMPTY alternative claims nothing
groups.why: the empty alternative must be dropped, not treated as a zero-length suffix that every path ends with — a matcher that kept it would have one member claim BOTH files

groups.name: a whitespace-only declaration claims nothing
groups.why: the blank member has no candidate; it must not silently match the file the real member wants

groups.name: a COMPLETE backup copy of the bundle is refused
groups.why: the declaration-level ambiguity check refuses BEFORE the root rule is consulted — two candidates per member

groups.name: a PARTIAL backup copy still groups — the root rule's stated LIMIT
groups.why: roots [run] and [run,backup] CHAIN, so the live and backed-up parts group together. Recorded as a measured fact rather than a comment: the chain is a NECESSARY condition, and tightening it would need the declaration to say what the bundle root is
